features.description: Auth profile contract, immutable registry, and secret-safe values
acceptance_criteria: AuthProfileRef, SafeProfile, AuthProfilePolicy, ProfileLease, LeaseMode, and AuthProfileBroker exist with the design doc's frozen semantics
All ten browser_auth_* failure categories are defined, unique, and distinct from the existing browser_* set
SensitiveProfileMaterial redacts under String, Error, MarshalJSON, %v, %+v, and %#v; Materialize is the only extraction path
Registry versions are immutable: republish fails, latest resolves to a concrete version, revoked and expired resolve to terminal structured failures
BrowserRunManifest carries alias, profile hash, and resolved version, and never serializes latest, cookies, object references, or provider context IDs
Existing non-authenticated browser tests pass unmodified
features.notes: Contract, immutable registry, and redaction shipped. Package deliberately does not import internal/browser so the dependency stays one-way; a parity test in internal/browser pins the two Redacted constants together. latest resolves by publish sequence, not version-string order, and an expired latest surfaces browser_auth_profile_expired rather than not_found so the operator gets an actionable signal. Existing browser tests passed unmodified. make test exit 0, lint clean, boundaries clean, file sizes clean.

features.description: Local encrypted storage-state materialization and destruction
acceptance_criteria: Envelope adapter seals and opens with a per-blob nonce; tampered ciphertext fails closed as browser_auth_materialize_failed
Materialized file is 0600 inside a 0700 session-owned directory, asserted on mode bits
Local provider passes --storage-state alongside --isolated; contents and canonical object reference never enter argv or the MCP config
Destruction is idempotent across success, error, cancellation, and timeout, and a cleanup failure does not mask the primary failure
Two-run isolation test proves run one's mutation is invisible to run two
Startup orphan audit removes stale materializations and records a structured audit event
features.notes: AES-256-GCM envelope with a fresh DEK and nonce per seal, header bound in as GCM additional data so a substituted key id or downgraded version reads as tampering. Tamper test flips one bit at every byte offset and requires each to fail closed with nil plaintext. RunOutcome keeps primary and cleanup failures in separate fields so masking cannot be the default. Storage-state path is a provider-local attachment type, NOT a browser.SessionSpec field, because SessionSpec crosses the serialization boundary. Windows skips POSIX mode-bit assertions (Go reports 0666/0444 there regardless of ACL). Agent verified non-vacuity against six deliberate mutations.

features.description: Browserbase Context adapter with non-persisting ordinary sessions
acceptance_criteria: Context create, get, and delete go through the injectable bounded HTTP client with no new unbounded path
Ordinary sessions send persist:false and only refresh mode sends persist:true; a read-mode persist request is refused as browser_auth_writeback_denied before any HTTP request
Context IDs are absent from SessionSpec, BrowserRunManifest, JSON, logs, and errors, asserted on containing structs
Stub tests cover auth failure, quota, malformed response, timeout, synchronization delay, expiry, and deletion
The live contract test stays credential-gated and is not a CI dependency
features.notes: Context create/get/delete on the existing injectable bounded client via a new doJSONWithStatus that exposes the status code, so a 404 on delete is success and retryable provider errors stay separable from terminal profile errors. ContextAttachment keeps the caller's Persist request separate from the lease Mode so the dangerous pairing stays expressible and testable; it is refused as browser_auth_writeback_denied before any request is built. Sync delay is an injectable waiter, not a sleep. Agent caught its own first redaction test being vacuous (an injected exported RawID field also passed) and replaced it with structural assertions. Also fixed a PRE-EXISTING leak: %#v on *Provider printed the API key verbatim. LIVE Browserbase contract test NOT run - no credentials on this machine; reported as skipped, never passed.

features.description: Lease, account pool, policy preflight, and audit
acceptance_criteria: Lease acquisition is compare-and-set; refresh mode is exclusive, read mode is bounded by MaxConcurrent, and conflict returns browser_auth_lease_conflict deterministically
Account-pool allocation gives distinct profiles per worker and exhaustion is a deterministic structured failure, never silent reuse
Preflight rejects missing, expired, revoked, scope-denied, artifact-denied, and takeover-denied profiles before a browser is provisioned, asserted by a fake provider that fails if called
An authenticated session with no artifact policy or no egress boundary is denied, and the denial names which policy was absent
The lease is released on success, error, cancellation, timeout, and panic, proven by a -race test with parallel workers
Audit events carry alias, profile hash, version, lease safe ID, principal, run/chain/stage, allowed origins, mode, decision, and timestamps, and no secrets
features.notes: Two parts. Part 1 (pure): compare-and-set leases proven by a 32-worker race test asserting EXACTLY MaxConcurrent grants; refresh exclusive against every mode; expired leases swept before the conflict decision so a crashed run cannot wedge a profile; account-pool exhaustion is structured, never silent reuse; preflight check order fixed and pinned by a test that breaks every policy then repairs them one at a time; AuditEvent safe structurally (reflection test fails if a secret-capable or []byte field is added). Part 2 (broker + controller): Provision resolves, matches provider, preflights, leases, materializes - and releases the lease if materialization fails. StartAuthenticated refuses a provider lacking CreateAuthenticated rather than silently downgrading to a logged-out session. Run.Use finishes on success, error, cancellation, deadline, and panic (re-panics rather than swallowing). Verified non-vacuous against three mutations: dropped lease release, preflight-after-acquire, and removed teardown - each was caught. Also fixed a data race in the SHARED test fake (unguarded calls slice) that any concurrent controller test would have hit.

features.description: Bootstrap and refresh CLI, eval wiring, operator guide, and repository gates
acceptance_criteria: bootstrap runs headful with recording disabled and marks the session non-comparable; it is never an eval
A site-adapter interface exists for trusted automated refresh and no generic model-driven password form filler ships, asserted by a test that no path passes a secret into an MCP tool argument
refresh publishes a new immutable version only after post-login verification under an exclusive lease, retires the old version, and records a rollback pointer
--browser-profile alias@version selects a profile in eval-suite and results record the resolved concrete version, never latest
The operator guide covers local keychain/1Password and Cloud Run Secret Manager/KMS, incident response, account pools, and the rotation drill
make test, lint, fmt-check, check-boundaries, and check-file-sizes pass, and the docs site builds
features.notes: Shipped: auth.LoginAdapter/PageDriver/SecretValue + broker Refresh/Bootstrap; FileRegistry (durable, 0600 under 0700, immutable versions, revoke/retire/purge); FileAuditSink (JSONL); `ailang browser-profile` with bootstrap/inspect/revoke/purge/audit/gc/refresh; --browser-profile wired through eval-suite into StartAuthenticated; operator guide; help.go. SCOPE NARROWING, AC1: AILANG does NOT drive a headful browser for bootstrap. The operator captures the storage state themselves with pinned Playwright MCP and passes --state-file, which is stronger on the stated goal (the password never enters AILANG at all) but is NOT what the AC literally says. The command prints the exact headful capture recipe. AC3 (refresh) is implemented and tested at the broker; the CLI `refresh` subcommand fails loudly because no reviewed site adapter ships - by design, not omission. Storage backend chosen per the design doc's deferred decision: local file tree under ~/.ailang/browser-profiles. Key protector stays pluggable (local file default, KMS behind the same interface) because that one is explicitly a human decision at deployment review. Verified: full make test exit 0, -race clean, lint 0 issues, gofmt clean, check-boundaries OK, check-file-sizes OK, GOOS=windows build+vet OK, and a real end-to-end CLI smoke run (bootstrap -> inspect -> revoke -> purge -> gc) confirming sealed-at-rest material, 0600/0700 permissions, and an audit trail.
